questions.stem: A Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) adds beyond stateful inspection:

choices.D: Deep packet inspection, application identification, and intrusion prevention

questions.explanation: NGFWs inspect application-layer content, identify applications by behaviour, and include integrated IPS functionality.
ACLs evaluate rules sequentially top-to-bottom; the first matching rule is applied and processing stops.

questions.stem: A screened subnet (dual-firewall DMZ) requires an attacker to:

choices.A: Compromise one firewall to reach the internal network
choices.B: Compromise both firewalls to reach the internal LAN from the internet

questions.explanation: A screened subnet places two firewalls around the DMZ, both must be compromised for an attacker to reach the internal network.

choices.C: Inspecting HTTP/HTTPS content to detect web attacks like SQLi, XSS, and CSRF

questions.explanation: A WAF operates at the application layer, detecting web attack patterns that network firewalls cannot see.

questions.stem: Implicit deny at the end of a firewall ACL means:

choices.A: All traffic is allowed unless explicitly denied
choices.C: Traffic not matching any permit rule is automatically blocked
choices.D: Only inbound traffic is denied by default

questions.explanation: Implicit deny implements default-deny security, anything not explicitly permitted is dropped automatically.

questions.stem: Egress filtering controls traffic that is:

choices.B: Leaving the network toward external destinations

questions.explanation: Egress filtering controls outbound traffic, preventing data exfiltration and stopping compromised hosts from contacting C2 servers.

questions.stem: The most precise firewall rule implementing least privilege allows:

choices.A: Any source to any destination on any port
choices.B: One specific source to one specific destination on one specific port
choices.C: Any internal host to any external host on HTTPS
choices.D: All internal and blocks all external traffic

questions.explanation: Least privilege in firewall rules means allowing only the exact required traffic, specific source, destination, and port.

questions.stem: Blocking Telnet (port 23) while allowing SSH (port 22) implements:

choices.C: Preference for encrypted over cleartext management protocols

questions.explanation: SSH encrypts the session; Telnet sends credentials in plaintext. This rule prevents management traffic from being intercepted.

choices.A: Serve as a production backup during attacks
choices.B: Attract and log attacker techniques without risking real systems

questions.explanation: Honeypots are decoy systems, any traffic to them is suspicious. Defenders study attacker tactics while protecting real systems.

choices.A: All traffic is permitted unless explicitly blocked
choices.B: All traffic is blocked unless explicitly permitted
choices.C: The most permissive matching rule is applied
choices.D: Outbound is allowed but inbound is denied by default

questions.explanation: Default-deny is the security best practice: explicitly permit only required traffic; block everything else.
